findings.result_name: What the doubling asks of a block's drive line (prop:ec-criterion)
findings.defect: The stated hypotheses do not entail the stated conclusion: nothing in them says WHICH pair of drive maps the identities of thm:ec-identity compare, and read literally the proposition closes the route's own declared GAP. GAP, exactly: the proposition needs the extra hypothesis "the target's outer bits force f_low(p) > f_high(p) at some p lying in the low windows, where f_low is the map whose fixed point is confined below b at sigma_lo and f_high the map, paired with it by one of the two identities, whose fixed point is confined above a at sigma_hi".
findings.evidence: In the swapped labelling of the second shape (the route's own GAP, rem:ec-scope) the very same block, the very same sigma_lo=4, sigma_hi=0, b=47723619/255897160, a=1175936917/2026652880 satisfy the proposition's hypotheses -- for z=8 the drives w00,w10,w11 are confined to LOW and w01 to HIGH (recomputed in my swapped.py: orders w00<w10<w11<w01 at sigma in {0,2,4,5,6} and w11<w10<w00<w01 at sigma in {1,3,7}) -- and M <= m holds over this block (my domin.py: least margin 0.009743). So the proposition as written would exclude z=8 in the swapped labelling, which the route itself states is unproved. The only step that fails there is the one the argument asserts in a clause ("since the identities force the low map to exceed the high map at a point of the low windows"): at p = w11 the identities leave f00(p) > f10(p) between two maps BOTH confined to LOW.

findings.result_name: thm:escape-no-beta is sharp: the second shape revives the beta-doublings (cor:ec-no-beta-fails)
findings.defect: "The hypothesis ... cannot be dropped" and "the second shape revives the beta-doublings" are not proved. What is proved is only that thm:escape-no-beta's PROOF mechanism (the three-comparison tournament of w00,w10,w01) no longer excludes anything once A''>0; no game, and no orientation realisable by any block, is exhibited for which thm:escape-no-beta's CONCLUSION fails. GAP, exactly: there exists a nondegenerate stopping generalised escape extension with A''>0, of some driven block, whose improvement outmap is B_phi(s,z')(.^zeta) with zeta_beta = 1.
findings.evidence: Over the only block examined the doublings are NOT revived: the route's own thm:ec-main proves z=24 and z=26 are still impossible for A''>0 over the level-two block (I reproduced both: z=26 loses 19 of 32 drives to empty windows, z=24 dies by the domination chain). So the corollary's title and first sentence assert the opposite of what the route proves three results later, for the only block in evidence. The verified content is the weaker, combinatorial statement I did reproduce (target.py, swapped.py): for each z in {8,10,24,26} and each of the 8 inner strategies the eight demanded outer bits are the edge comparisons of a total order of the four drives (z=8: w00<w01<w11<w10 / w11<w01<w00<w10; z=24: w01<w00<w10<w11 / w10<w00<w01<w11), and the antipodal complementarities hold, so the tournament excludes nothing.

findings.result_name: The level theorem for the second escape shape (thm:ec-level2)
findings.defect: The displayed table of eight outer bits is FALSE on part of the hypothesis class the route's own def:ec-escape2 admits, namely A''=0: there O_alpha(0,1)=[w01<w11] is identically 0 because w01=w11, whereas the true bit is thm:escape-level's S=[rho(sigma,w01)>0], which is 1 at some strategies. The theorem needs A''>0 in the hypothesis of the display (the following sentence half-acknowledges this by saying the two alpha-bits "degenerate", but the theorem is stated for every generalised escape extension).
findings.evidence: The paper's own realisation is a counterexample. Files: control_b2.py, nf.py. Nothing else depends on this: thm:ec-main's proof handles A''=0 separately through S.

findings.result_name: The domination lemma on the level-two drive line (lem:ec-domination)
findings.defect: The description of the refinement is wrong in the count, though harmlessly so: "the 13 fences of the drive line and the 6 further switches of the block's Min vertex cut [0,1]" into "20 refined pieces" (and "21 breakpoints" elsewhere). There are exactly 3 distinct drives at which the block's Min vertex switches, so 16 interior breakpoints and 17 pieces.
findings.evidence: block.py/drive.py/affine.py: tau-crossings at 163841371/5307039440, 515451615/2447540677 and 33981/55658 (the last shared by sigma=3 and sigma=7); y_sigma verified affine on each of the 17 pieces by second differences at six interior points per piece per sigma. The route's ec_block.py adds roots of margins evaluated at the NON-optimal tau, which are not breakpoints of y_sigma; its partition is therefore a strict refinement and the argument is unaffected -- and on [0,T] the two branch-point sets coincide exactly (0, eight fences, three tau switches, T = 13 points, giving the route's 8x13 = 104 pairs).

findings.result_name: No escape extension of the level-two block doubles (thm:ec-main)
findings.defect: The proof asserts, without argument, that "the order relations of cor:ec-no-beta-fails prune the second component at sigma=3,7". The one-line justification is missing from the write-up.
findings.evidence: I verified it (edge.py): LOW_3 = cells [0,1] u [9], LOW_7 = cells [0,1] u [9,10], and the extra components begin exactly at T = 10168377/16341335 = sup HIGH_3 = sup HIGH_7, while in both targets every LOW drive is strictly below the unique HIGH drive, which is < T; hence every LOW drive lies in the first component. With this supplied, all the numerical inputs of the theorem check out: sup LOW_4 = b, inf HIGH_0 = a, sup LOW_sigma <= min(inf HIGH_sigma, T) for all eight sigma, LOW and HIGH cell sets disjoint, and no tied incidence at t=0 or t=1.

findings.result_name: The level theorem for the second escape shape (thm:ec-level2)
findings.defect: "acyclic, with sink at the largest drive and source at the smallest" asserts uniqueness of the sink of the outer square, which does not follow from the four drives alone: on a 2-cube, four reals with every edge pointing at the larger can have two local maxima (e.g. w00=4, w10=1, w01=2, w11=3 makes both (0,0) and (1,1) sinks). Uniqueness holds only by prop:allsw-auso (the improvement outmap of a nondegenerate stopping SSG is a USO), which the route does not cite here; conversely that gives a further necessary condition on the four drives which the route does not extract.
findings.evidence: Direct check of the route's own bit table O_alpha(0,0)=[w00<w10], O_beta(0,0)=[w00<w01], O_alpha(1,1)=1-[w01<w11], O_beta(1,1)=1-[w10<w11] on the displayed quadruple gives outmap 0 at both (0,0) and (1,1).

findings.result_name: What the doubling asks of a block's drive line (prop:ec-criterion)
findings.defect: The closed forms for M and m are obtained by STRONG linear-programming duality, an import beyond the paper's four permitted facts; only weak duality is needed for the criterion's use (any mu gives an upper bound on M, any nu a lower bound on m), and the criterion can be stated with the primal programmes alone.
findings.evidence: I re-derived both duals and confirmed the displayed formulas are the exact duals of the two three-constraint programmes; my own verification used the primal vertex enumeration (domin.py), which needs no duality at all and gives the same 104 values.

findings.defect: "over this block every escape shape, pinned or not, single- or double-reading, is now dead" overstates the route's own result and contradicts its GAP: the second shape with the exchanged labelling (alpha,beta) = (beta_2, alpha_2) is not dead over this block at z=8 or z=24.
findings.evidence: rem:ec-scope in the route's own LaTeX states exactly that this case is open; my swapped.py confirms both z=8 and z=24 pass the tournament and the inner condition there.

verdict:
The route's central mathematics is correct and reproduces exactly; two of its five results are over-stated, one of them in a way that would settle the route's own declared gap, so sound = false.
